info.title: Reporting source protocol
info.summary: What a source product implements so that the reporting platform's adapter `http` reads it (S19-A; revision 1.1 adds the optional companies route, S19-B, and a dataset's optional filters and sorts declarations with a query's filters and sort, S20-A, ADR 0023).
info.description: docs/SOURCE_HTTP_PROTOCOL.md is the prose reference and wins where they differ; TestTheOpenAPIDescriptionIsTheProtocol (adapters/httpsource) holds this file to the bodies the adapter sends and accepts. Every request is POST with a JSON body of at most 1 MiB; every answer is application/json of at most 1 MiB, one object, no unknown field, no null, no duplicate key, nothing after it. Values are strings where the platform has exact decimals. The issue routes are needed only for a connection whose issuance is rows or groups; the companies route only for a connection with companies true (ADR 0015). A dataset may declare filters and sorts (S20-A); a query then carries them, and the source applies them as parameters.

401.description: The service credential is missing or wrong (no body needed). The platform treats it as unavailable.

bearer.description: The platform's service credential, from the environment variable the connection's auth_env names.

RequestID.name: X-Request-Id
RequestID.description: The platform's random id of this request. Log it.

platform_tenant.description: The platform tenant of the verified access token.

subject.description: The access token's subject. The source maps (platform_tenant, issuer, subject) to its own actor; nothing else of a request is an authority.

Context.description: Who asks, through which connection. platform_tenant + issuer + subject at most 1024 bytes together.

scale.description: Decimal places of a decimal, 0..18; absent for the other types.

columns.description: The dimensions, then the metrics, in their order.

filters.description: The columns a query of this version may narrow by, with their operators (ADR 0023). A field at most once. Absent: no filter is accepted.

sorts.description: The columns a query of this version may order by, with their directions. A field at most once. Absent: no sort is accepted.

Dataset.description: A published dataset version. The lists of filters and sorts are part of the version, as the columns are: a change is a new version.

field.description: A column id of the dataset.

operators.description: A non-empty set of the closed operators that fit the column's type: prefix and contains for string columns only; lt, le, gt, ge, between and in for date, integer, decimal and string; a boolean column takes eq and ne only.

values.description: Optional: the closed list of values the field accepts, each well formed for the column; an eq, ne or in filter must take its values from it.

required.description: true: a query must carry exactly one filter on this field (a mandatory parameter).

FilterSpec.description: One filter a dataset version publishes (reporting.FilterSpec).

field.description: A column id of the dataset.

SortSpec.description: One sort key a dataset version publishes (reporting.SortSpec).

field.description: A field the dataset version declares a filter on.

operator.description: One of the operators declared for the field.

value.description: The value, well formed for the column (a date YYYY-MM-DD, an integer or a decimal as the column writes it, true or false, a string of 1..128 characters without control characters), from the declared closed list when there is one. For in and between a JSON array of such strings as text, ["a","b"]: 1..32 values for in, exactly 2 in ascending order for between. The source binds it as a parameter, never as text of a statement.

Filter.description: One filter of a query (reporting.Filter). A query's filters are a conjunction, sorted by field, operator and value in the normalized query.

field.description: A field the dataset version declares a sort on; no field twice in a query.

Sort.description: One sort key of a query (reporting.Sort), in the order the keys apply.

filters.description: The query's filters, each on a field and with an operator the dataset version declares (ADR 0023); the platform has validated them against the catalog it read, and a source refuses what it did not publish with unsupported. Empty for a query that narrows nothing.

sort.description: The query's sort keys, in the order they apply, each on a field and in a direction the dataset version declares; no field twice. Empty: the source's own order.

QuerySpec.description: The platform's query (docs/API.md), as the caller sent it, company_ids sorted. company_ids are selectors, never an authority.

ref.description: The source's reference of the read; also the path segment.

scope_handle.description: Opaque to the platform, 1..1024 printable ASCII.

query_hash.description: The query_hash of the request, repeated.

company_ids.description: Exactly the query's, in its order.

watermark.description: The version of the source data the read is frozen at, 1..256 printable ASCII.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 in the form Go's time.RFC3339Nano writes (no trailing zeros in a fraction); the platform sends a read's expires_at back exactly as it was given. After the platform's now, at most 15 minutes ahead.

Read.description: A prepared read. The platform keeps it and sends every field back unchanged in later requests; the source must check it against its own record.

datasets.description: The published versions the context may read now; at most 100, no reference twice.

id.description: The value a query names in company_ids: 1..128 bytes of UTF-8 text without control characters, no id twice in a list.

name.description: What a person reads: 1..128 bytes of UTF-8 text without control characters, not blank. The platform never stores it.

Company.description: One company the context may choose (ADR 0015).

companies.description: The companies the context may choose now, in the product's order; at most 1000. Empty is an answer: nothing may be chosen.

partial.description: True when the product cut the list (more than 1000, or its own bound); the person may still type an id.

CompaniesResponse.description: The directory's answer. The list is advisory: reads and authorize decide every read as without it.

query_hash.description: reporting.QueryHash of the query (SHA-256 of its JSON without page, companies sorted). The source may recompute it and refuse a mismatch (integrity).

cursor.description: "" for the first page, else the next_cursor of the previous page.

rows.description: At most limit rows, each of the dataset's columns, as exact strings.

totals.description: One total per metric of the dataset, the same on every page.

next_cursor.description: "" on the last page; else 1..2048 printable ASCII, never the request's cursor, never after an empty page.

authorized.description: Only true is an authorization; a refusal is an error.

row_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the row's JSON as docs/API.md specifies; "" for a group intent.

issued_at.description: RFC 3339 in the form Go's time.RFC3339Nano writes (no trailing zeros in a fraction); the platform sends a read's expires_at back exactly as it was given. A whole second, 1970..9999.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 in the form Go's time.RFC3339Nano writes (no trailing zeros in a fraction); the platform sends a read's expires_at back exactly as it was given. After issued_at.

confirmed_at.description: RFC 3339 in the form Go's time.RFC3339Nano writes (no trailing zeros in a fraction); the platform sends a read's expires_at back exactly as it was given. A whole second, not before issued_at.

reason.description: The platform's reason (an error code), UTF-8, at most 1024 bytes.

Error.description: Every refusal's body, sent with the code's own status (docs/SOURCE_HTTP_PROTOCOL.md, Errors).
